domain: daily range geometry and return-shape information from daily OHLCV (range-based volatility used for cross-sectional RISK pricing, not trend)
title: Range-based cross-sectional risk pricing: beta-neutral long low Garman-Klass range-volatility sector ETFs versus high range-volatility sector ETFs

mechanism.causal_economic: Leverage constraints and benchmark constraints cause a systematic class of investors to over-allocate to visibly risky assets: they cannot lever low-risk assets to their desired return, so they bid high-risk assets above fundamental risk-neutral value, and accept inferior risk-adjusted returns on them (Black 1972 constraint story; Frazzini-Pedersen 2014 betting-against-beta; Baker-Bradley-Wurgler 2011). The premium is therefore earned BY the low-risk side and paid BY the high-risk side, and it is a cross-sectional relative premium, not a market-timing effect. For the observable, we measure 'risk' with an intraday range estimator rather than close-to-close volatility: Garman-Klass (1980) combines open/high/low/close within each session and is roughly 5-7.4x more efficient than the close-to-close estimator under a diffusion, so at a fixed 63-session window it ranks the true relative risk of sector ETFs with less sampling noise, which matters in an 11-name cross-section where rank noise directly destroys the spread. The trade prices RELATIVE risk across the 11 sector ETFs; it never times the market.
mechanism.after_cost_rationale: Documented low-risk/BAB spreads at index-member and asset-class granularity are of order several percent per year risk-adjusted (Frazzini-Pedersen 2014 report multi-percent annualized BAB spreads; Baker-Bradley-Wurgler document several percent between low- and high-vol quintiles). Expected cost drag at 10 bps/side with ~2-4 two-way turnover per year is roughly 25-80 bps per year, one to two orders of magnitude below the documented anomaly scale, so a real premium should survive after-cost; a borderline anomaly should not, which is the discriminating property we want.
mechanism.falsifiable_prediction: Sign: NEGATIVE cross-sectional relation between trailing 63-session Garman-Klass variance and forward beta-adjusted relative returns of sector ETFs. Operationally: the anchor book (long the 3 lowest GK-variance sector ETFs, short the 3 highest, SPY-beta-neutralized, 42-session holding) must show (i) after-cost expectancy > 0, (ii) positive incremental alpha versus its declared risk-matched SPY context overall and in >= 2 of 3 folds, (iii) its mirror (long-high/short-low) must NOT show the same. If GK ranks are pure noise, expectancy concentrates near 0 or the mirror also 'works' (unstable sign), and the control gate fires.
mechanism.distinctness: Not a descendant of any forbidden family: (1) NOT sector momentum (A4_XSEC_ETF_RELATIVE_MOMENTUM): the ranking key contains no return level, no return sign, and no price trend - Garman-Klass variance is built from within-day log(H/L) and log(C/O) magnitudes only and is sign-blind by construction, so the arm cannot encode 'buy recent winners'; vol ranks and return ranks are different orderings and the beta hedge removes the common market leg that carried the V2 momentum control. (2) NOT trend/defensive rotation (A5-SFV2-TREND-DEFENSIVE): there is no SMA, no time-series trend filter, and no volatility TARGETING - gross exposure is a frozen constant (0.5 long + 0.5 short + bounded hedge leg) and never scales with realized vol; the arm is always fully in the market with a fixed dollar-neutral, beta-neutral shape, so it cannot 'defend' by de-risking. (3) NOT idiosyncratic shock reversal (SFV3-A6): it holds no position conditional on any shock event, uses no return-level or overshoot statistic, and holds for 42 sessions cross-sectionally rather than fading a nearby daily shock. (4) NOT calendar: the rebalance grid is a fixed session-count cadence with no claim about dates. (5) The sort variable is an input to risk PRICING (which relative risk earns a premium), explicitly the 'range or volatility-shape information not reducible to trend' direction allowed by PLAN_stocks_v4.md section 2.

primary_sources: Frazzini, A. and Pedersen, L.H. (2014), 'Betting Against Beta', Journal of Financial Economics 111(1), 1-25 - constraint-driven overpricing of risky assets and the levered-low-beta premium.

Baker, M., Bradley, B. and Wurgler, J. (2011), 'Benchmarks as Limits to Arbitrage: Understanding the Low-Volatility Anomaly', Financial Analysts Journal 67(1), 40-54 - why low-volatility assets outperform high-volatility assets risk-adjusted.

Garman, M.B. and Klass, M.J. (1980), 'On the Estimation of Security Price Volatilities from Historical Data', Journal of Business 53(1), 67-78 - the OHLC range-based variance estimator used as the ranking key (Parkinson 1980 extreme-value estimator is the neighbour variant).

fields_used: {SYM}_none_p1.json fields: open, high, low, close (RAW as-traded prices) - used ONLY for within-day Garman-Klass terms ln(H_t/L_t) and ln(C_t/O_t) of the 11 sector ETFs; declared ex ante per p2_a3_data_manifest.json raw_vs_total_return_authorization (raw series remains authorized for price-level features where declared ex ante; within-day ratios contain no distribution effect and are never used for returns)
{SYM}_all_p1.json fields: close (adjusted) - for sector-ETF close-to-close betas (hedge sizing) and for all portfolio return computation
SPY_all_p1.json fields: close (adjusted) - hedge-instrument beta (=1 by definition), risk-matched SPY benchmark context per p2_a3_benchmark_contract.json
authorized_pit_inputs.fields_not_used: volume, distribution records, split factors (2025-12-05 splits are after S0 and never read), and all unavailable-field classes (fundamentals, earnings, borrow, short interest, holdings, flows, options, intraday bars)
authorized_pit_inputs.windows: S0 screening window 2018-04-04..2025-07-31; warmup <= 252 sessions before the first scored session taken from the 2076-session pre-S0 runway (2010-01-04..2018-04-03); no session after 2025-07-31 is read or scored
authorized_pit_inputs.availability_rule: XLC enters the eligible ranking set only once it has >= 252 sessions of history (from ~2019-06); before that the rank set is the eligible members present - a fixed availability rule declared ex ante, not a selection choice

universe_and_schedule.universe: the 11 sector ETFs of the frozen cohort (cohort minus SPY); SPY is used only as hedge instrument and benchmark context, never ranked
universe_and_schedule.warmup_sessions: 252 (beta window) with a 63-session Garman-Klass window nested inside it; first decision uses sessions 2017-04-05..2018-04-04
universe_and_schedule.decision_clock: at the close (PIT) of every 42nd SPY-calendar session within S0, first decision at the first S0 session 2018-04-04; only information through that close is used
universe_and_schedule.holding_period: 42 sessions per decision; weights held unchanged between decisions; book forced flat at every fold boundary per baseline invariants (a decision shortly before a boundary holds a truncated stub)
universe_and_schedule.fill_clock: next allowed session after the decision close, open-adjacent close-to-close execution per baseline invariants ADJ-1-EXEC-CLOCK; no same-session fill

anchor.name: GK63-BN-L3S3-42
anchor.rule: At each decision session d: (1) for every eligible sector ETF i (>= 252 sessions of history through d, availability rule above), compute GK variance gk_i(d) = (1/63) * sum over the last 63 available sessions t of [ 0.5*(ln(H_t/L_t))^2 - (2*ln(2)-1)*(ln(C_t/O_t))^2 ] using RAW as-traded OHLC of session t only; if a session has a non-positive or zero-range price making a log term undefined, that session is dropped from the mean and the window refills backward (frozen rule); (2) rank eligible sectors ASCENDING by gk_i(d); (3) long the 3 lowest at +1/6 weight each, short the 3 highest at -1/6 weight each; (4) estimate beta_i(d) by OLS of sector i adjusted close-to-close daily returns on SPY adjusted close-to-close daily returns over the last 252 sessions through d, and set the hedge leg w_SPY(d) = -sum_i(w_i * beta_i), truncated to [-0.25, +0.25]; (5) residual weight to CASH; frozen gross cap 1.25; long/short books accounted separately per baseline invariants; no other rule exists. Ranking uses raw gk variance (annualization is a monotone transform and cannot change the rank, so it is not applied).
anchor.exactness: single estimator (Garman-Klass), single window (63), single holding (42), single beta window (252), single basket size (3+3), single weight (1/6), single truncation ([-0.25,+0.25]) - no parameter menu, no grid, no best-of

neighbour.name: PK63-BN-L3S3-42
neighbour.rule: Identical to the anchor in every fixed choice except the estimator: rank by Parkinson (1980) range variance pk_i(d) = (1/(4*ln(2)*63)) * sum over the last 63 sessions of (ln(H_t/L_t))^2 (same raw OHLC, same eligibility, same 3+3 baskets, same beta hedge, same 42-session grid). Parkinson uses only the high-low extreme-value term, so agreement between anchor and neighbour demonstrates the premium attaches to the range-risk mechanism rather than to one estimator's open-close term.
neighbour.role: mechanism support required by stage-A gates (neighbour_mechanism_support)

causal_negative_control.name: ALPHA3-BN-L3S3-42 (alphabetical-ticker control)
causal_negative_control.rule: Identical surface form: same 42-session grid, same 3+3 baskets at +/-1/6, same 252-session beta hedge, same accounting - but the ranking key is alphabetical ticker order of the eligible cohort members (XLB, XLC, XLE, ... XLV, XLY), i.e. always long the 3 alphabetically-first eligible sectors and short the 3 alphabetically-last. Ticker alphabet has no causal channel to forward sector returns.
causal_negative_control.must_not_carry_mechanism_if_story_true: If the constraint/lottery risk-pricing story is true, a book whose composition is determined by ticker spelling carries no risk premium and its expectancy is statistically zero.
causal_negative_control.preregistered_falsification_rule: The anchor is REJECTED if the control's incremental alpha satisfies |alpha_control| >= 0.5 * |alpha_anchor| (control_alpha_abs_ratio gate, baseline invariants), or if control expectancy > 0 with per-position PF >= 1.0. Either outcome means the beta-neutral L/S surface form itself, not the range-risk ranking, generated the anchor result; the mechanism class is then falsified for this universe and no rescue variant may be proposed.

factor_alpha_test.primary: incremental alpha per p2_a3_benchmark_contract.json: incremental_alpha(arm, window) = R_arm(window) - R_spy_context(window), evaluated per fold AND overall on S0; the arm's frozen ex-ante risk-match declaration is ZERO SPY-context multiple, because the construction zeroes net SPY beta by rule via the hedge leg (declared before any return is computed; realized arm volatility or realized beta is never substituted post hoc); a pass requires positive incremental alpha overall and in >= 2 folds per stage-A gates
factor_alpha_test.sector_neutralization: the optional equal-weight sector factor (EW_SECTOR_TOTAL_RETURN per the benchmark contract) is reported as a secondary residual diagnostic: regress arm daily returns on [SPY context, EW-sector context]; the residual mean must be positive per fold. Caveat declared ex ante: the legs ARE members of the EW-sector factor, so the SPY risk-match is the primary identifiying test and the EW-sector residual is diagnostic only
factor_alpha_test.fail_closed: raw PnL, long-equity beta, or sector beta is never accepted as alpha; FLAT_HARD_BENCHMARK (0% floor) also applies per contract

costs_and_turnover.costs: 10 bps per side per fill (base), 20 bps per side (stress rerun), charged exactly once per fill per P1-A2 invariant; benchmark paths uncosted per contract
costs_and_turnover.expected_turnover: rebalances: 6 per year (42-session grid). GK range-vol ranks are persistent (volatility clustering), so average expected membership churn is ~1-2 of 6 basket legs per rebalance: expected |delta_weight| per rebalance ~0.4-0.8 including the hedge-leg drift, giving ~2.0-4.0 two-way turnover per year annualized
costs_and_turnover.why_inside_ceiling: expected 2.0-4.0 two-way/year is below the 6.0 ceiling with margin; the theoretical worst case (all 6 legs reconstituted every rebalance, ~12-13 two-way/year) would itself evidence that range-vol ranks carry no stable information and would fail the turnover gate by design - we accept that gate as part of the falsification structure rather than loosening the schedule
costs_and_turnover.cost_drag: ~25-80 bps/year at base, ~50-160 bps/year at stress; the documented anomaly scale (several percent risk-adjusted per year) dominates this only if the premium truly exists at sector-ETF granularity, which is exactly what the test decides

sample_size_floor.decisions_per_fold: ~14-15 decisions per fold (1842 S0 sessions / 42-session grid, truncated at fold boundaries); each fold >= 5 floor satisfied
sample_size_floor.decisions_total: ~43-44 scored decision periods overall; >= 30 floor satisfied
sample_size_floor.positions_per_decision: 6 sector legs + 1 SPY hedge leg + CASH residual; >= 1 non-CASH leg invariant always satisfied

drop_one_design.expected_concentration: no single leg exceeds 1/6 (~16.7%) of gross, under the 0.35 per-symbol positive-share gate; the book is a portfolio order statistic over 11 persistent-vol names, so any single sector's contribution to expectancy is expected to be well under 25%
drop_one_design.drop_one_etf: rerun the full value book excluding the max-contribution symbol (10 eligible sectors; long-3/short-3 and hedge unchanged); survival = after-drop expectancy > 0; because baskets are thirds of a persistent ordering, dropping one name shifts at most one basket slot and the premium should survive if it is a cross-sectional risk premium rather than a single-name artifact
drop_one_design.drop_one_fold: min over folds of expectancy with that fold removed; survival = min > 0; the three folds span structurally different regimes (2018-2020 includes Volmageddon and the COVID crash, 2020-2023 the inflation/rate shock, 2023-2025 the AI-concentration rally), so a genuine risk premium should not depend on any single regime

failure_interpretation: A reject means the low-risk/BAB premium documented in single stocks and asset classes does not transmit to beta-neutral cross-sectional RISK pricing of sector ETFs at 63-session/42-session horizons after costs - the constraint-driven overpricing story is either absent at ETF granularity or too small relative to 10-20 bps costs. It also closes the range-estimator refinement direction for this universe: if the premium is not there, no Parkinson/GK/RS estimator choice can rescue it, and A7-N should treat estimator-swap variants of this skeleton as descendants of a rejected family.
source_to_test_map: 1. Frazzini-Pedersen (2014) / Baker-Bradley-Wurgler (2011): constrained investors overpay for risky assets -> implement as cross-sectional sort on measured risk with long-low-risk / short-high-risk baskets (anchor step 2-3).

2. Black (1972) leverage-constraint premium is about RELATIVE risk, not market direction -> implement SPY beta neutralization with a 252-session OLS hedge leg (anchor step 4) and declare zero SPY-context in the incremental-alpha test.

3. Garman-Klass (1980): OHLC range estimator is ~5-7.4x more efficient than close-to-close variance -> implement gk_i(d) from raw within-day OHLC over 63 sessions as the ranking key (anchor step 1), with Parkinson (1980) as the single estimator-swap neighbour.

4. Anomaly must survive real trading costs -> apply frozen 10 bps/side base and 20 bps stress on ~2-4 two-way/year turnover, evaluate incremental alpha vs risk-matched SPY per the frozen benchmark contract (factor_alpha_test).

5. The mechanism is cross-sectional pricing, not timing -> fixed gross, no vol targeting, no trend filter, fixed 42-session grid; alphabetical control detects any residual surface-form artifact (causal_negative_control).

implementation_estimate.risk_notes: (1) raw-OHLC hygiene: must confirm _none files carry genuine as-traded O/H/L/C and that no session has non-positive prices; zero-range sessions handled by the frozen drop-and-refill rule. (2) GK bias under jumps/gaps is accepted (both arms share it). (3) beta window overlaps S0 start via pre-S0 runway (2076 sessions available, ~8x need). (4) XLC availability handled by the declared fixed rule. (5) reuses existing V4 accounting (long/short books, CASH residual, cost-once, turnover convention) with no new infrastructure; largest engineering risk is correctly excluding CASH from turnover/concentration per baseline invariants.
